name: 囚徒困境
oneLiner: 各自选择对己最优的策略，结果却对双方都更差。
oneLinerEn: Each player choosing their best response leaves both worse off.
detail: 两名嫌疑人分开审讯，无论对方怎么选，认罪（背叛）都是自己的最优策略，于是双方都认罪并被重判——而如果都沉默，惩罚更轻。这个结构刻画了价格战、军备竞赛、公共资源过度使用与减排谈判等大量现实困境。关键在于：个体理性不等于集体理性。
detailEn: Two suspects interrogated separately both find confessing (defecting) strictly better whatever the other does, so both confess and both get heavier sentences — whereas mutual silence is better. The structure models price wars, arms races, overuse of common resources and climate negotiations. Individual rationality is not collective rationality.
example: 两家公司都降价抢份额，最终行业利润整体下滑，谁都不比默契维持价格时更好。
exampleEn: Two firms both cut prices to win share; industry profit falls and neither does better than under tacit price discipline.
takeaways: 需要重复博弈、可观察行为与惩罚机制，合作才可能稳定
制度设计的目标常常是改变收益结构，而非改变人性
takeawaysEn: Cooperation stabilises with repetition, observability and punishment
Institutional design usually changes payoffs rather than human nature

sources.label: 阿克塞尔罗德《合作的进化》

name: 纳什均衡
oneLiner: 人人都已选定策略，且无人能靠单方面改变而获益。
oneLinerEn: Everyone has chosen, and no one gains by changing alone.
detail: 纳什均衡是博弈解的基本概念，但它既不一定唯一，也不一定高效。多个均衡并存时，「谁先行动、如何沟通、历史与习惯」决定最终落点，这就是「协调问题」。混合策略均衡还意味着理性玩家会主动随机化，让对手无法预测。
detailEn: Nash equilibrium is the basic solution concept, but it need not be unique or efficient. With multiple equilibria, who moves first, how players communicate and history decide the outcome — a coordination problem. Mixed-strategy equilibria imply rational players deliberately randomise to stay unpredictable.
example: 键盘布局、充电接口标准、靠左还是靠右行驶，都是「多个均衡中选了一个」的协调结果。
exampleEn: Keyboard layouts, charging standards and driving sides are all coordination outcomes among multiple equilibria.
takeaways: 预测博弈结果需要额外信息：历史、沟通与信念
协调失败是真实成本，标准与惯例因此具有经济价值
takeawaysEn: Predicting outcomes needs extra information: history, communication and beliefs
Coordination failure is a real cost, so standards and conventions have economic value

sources.label: 纳什《n 人博弈的均衡点》
sources.labelEn: Nash, Equilibrium Points in n-Person Games

name: 智猪博弈
oneLiner: 强者去按按钮、弱者坐享其成，也会是稳定结果。
oneLinerEn: The strong press the button while the weak free-ride — and that can be stable.
detail: 在一个猪圈里，按按钮会带来食物但要付出成本。大猪食量大、抢食能力强，若不按就没得吃；小猪反正抢不过，最佳选择是等在食槽边。结果是「小猪搭便车、大猪承担成本」。这解释了为什么大企业常承担行业公共品（标准、渠道、政策游说），而小企业跟随。
detailEn: In the boxed-pigs setup, pressing the lever brings food but costs effort. The big pig eats more and must act or starve; the small pig cannot win the scramble and does best waiting. The equilibrium has the small pig free-riding and the big pig bearing cost — mirroring how large firms fund industry public goods while smaller ones follow.
example: 行业龙头发起标准化与合规建设，中小企业直接沿用，成本由龙头承担。
exampleEn: A market leader funds standards and compliance work while smaller firms simply adopt them.
takeaways: 「搭便车」不总是道德问题，而是收益结构决定的均衡
强者可通过改变规则（如许可、门槛）让弱者分担成本
takeawaysEn: Free-riding is often an equilibrium of payoffs, not a moral choice
The strong can redesign rules — licensing, thresholds — to share the cost

name: 公地悲剧
oneLiner: 收益归个人、成本由群体分担时，资源会被过度使用。
oneLinerEn: When benefits are private and costs shared, resources are overused.
detail: 牧场上每户多放一头牛，收益全归自己，草场退化成本由所有人分摊，于是每户都倾向增加放牧直到草场毁掉。这是多人版囚徒困境。出路包括私有权界定、配额与税费、以及奥斯特罗姆记录的自下而上的社区自治规则。
detailEn: Each herder gains fully from one more animal while degradation costs are shared, so everyone expands until the pasture is ruined: a multi-player prisoner's dilemma. Solutions include privatisation, quotas and taxes, and the bottom-up community rules documented by Ostrom.
example: 共享单车无约束投放、公海渔业枯竭、地下水超采，都是同一结构。
exampleEn: Unlimited dockless bikes, depleted high-seas fisheries and falling water tables share the same structure.
takeaways: 「共有」不等于「无主」，规则设计决定资源能否持续
总量控制（配额）往往比单纯价格干预更直接
takeawaysEn: 'Shared' does not mean 'unowned': rule design determines sustainability
Quantity caps are often more direct than price-only intervention

sources.label: 哈丁《公地悲剧》
sources.labelEn: Hardin, The Tragedy of the Commons

name: 胆小鬼博弈
oneLiner: 双方都硬撑到底就会同归于尽，先退让的一方反而「输」。
oneLinerEn: Both holding firm ends in mutual ruin, yet whoever swerves 'loses'.
detail: 两车对撞，先转向者被看作胆小鬼。由于让步代价高、相撞代价更高，玩家会用「自断退路」来提升可信度——例如公开承诺、销毁多余产能、让第三方见证。这也解释了危机边缘政策（brinkmanship）与部分贸易与地缘对抗。
detailEn: Two cars drive at each other; whoever swerves first is the coward. Because conceding is costly but colliding is worse, players raise credibility by removing their own retreat — public commitments, scrapping spare capacity, third-party witnesses. It explains brinkmanship and aspects of trade and geopolitical confrontation.
example: 谈判中公开宣称「绝不接受低于 X 的方案」，就是主动放弃让步空间，以提高威胁的可信度。
exampleEn: Publicly declaring 'no deal below X' voluntarily removes your room to concede, raising the credibility of your threat.
takeaways: 可信承诺需要真实成本，否则不被相信
博弈中「让自己没得选」有时是一种策略
takeawaysEn: Credible commitment needs real cost, or it is not believed
Sometimes removing your own options is the strategy

name: 重复博弈与合作
oneLiner: 当博弈会继续下去，合作就能成为稳定策略。
oneLinerEn: When the game continues, cooperation can become a stable strategy.
detail: 阿克塞尔罗德竞赛显示，「以牙还牙」——首轮合作、之后复制对方上一步——在长期重复博弈中表现极佳：它善意、可报复、可原谅且规则清晰。关键前提是未来足够重要（贴现因子高）、行为可观察、背叛会被惩罚。
detailEn: Axelrod's tournaments showed tit-for-tat — cooperate first, then mirror the opponent's last move — performs excellently in repeated play: nice, retaliatory, forgiving and clear. The preconditions are that the future matters enough, actions are observable and defection can be punished.
example: 同一条街上的老店更讲信用，因为还要长期做邻居；一次性旅游区的宰客则是另一种均衡。
exampleEn: Long-standing shops on the same street keep their word because they must live with their neighbours; tourist traps behave differently.
takeaways: 稳定关系本身就是一种执行力，能替代部分正式监管
匿名化、一次性交易会破坏合作的基础
takeawaysEn: A stable relationship is itself an enforcement device, partly replacing formal regulation
Anonymity and one-off transactions undermine the basis of cooperation

sources.label: 阿克塞尔罗德《合作的进化》

name: 拍卖与机制设计
oneLiner: 把规则设计好，自利的竞价者会自己透露私人估值——这是反过来的博弈：先设局，再让人择优。
oneLinerEn: Design the rules well and self-interested bidders reveal private values—it is games in reverse: set the stage, then let them optimize.
detail: 机制设计不问'给定规则如何博弈'，而问'要得到好结果该定什么规则'。拍卖是典范：英式增价、荷式降价、第一价格密封与维克瑞（第二价格）密封各有策略。维克瑞拍卖让出价等于真实估值成为占优策略，从而减少'赢家诅咒'与策略性压价。现实中无线电频谱、碳排放额度都用组合拍卖，还需防合谋与信息泄露。
detailEn: Mechanism design asks not 'given rules, how to play' but 'what rules yield good outcomes'. Auctions are the model: English ascending, Dutch descending, first-price sealed and Vickrey (second-price) sealed each carry distinct strategies. A Vickrey auction makes bidding your true value dominant, curbing the winner's curse and strategic shading. Real designs—spectrum, carbon allowances—use combinatorial auctions and must guard collusion and information leakage.
example: 美国 FCC 用多轮升价组合拍卖分配频谱，让电信运营商在互补牌照间自动报出高价值组合。
exampleEn: The US FCC's simultaneous multiple-round auction allocates spectrum, letting carriers bid high-value license packages.
takeaways: 规则本身塑造行为：好的设计让说真话成为最优。
不同拍卖格式对应不同风险，理解'赢家诅咒'才能避免过激报价。
takeawaysEn: The rules shape behaviour: good design makes truth-telling optimal.
Formats carry different risks; grasp the winner's curse to avoid overbidding.

sources.label: 维克瑞《反投机、竞争与社会组织》；米尔格罗姆《拍卖理论导论》

name: 协调博弈与路径依赖
oneLiner: 多个均衡里，大家各选一边都能过，却可能集体锁死在更差的惯例上，且越久越难改。
oneLinerEn: With several equilibria, either side works for all, yet the crowd can lock into a worse convention that grows harder to change.
detail: 与囚徒困境不同，协调博弈里个人利益与集体利益同向，问题是'往哪边协调'。键盘 QWERTY、技术标准、货币单位、语言习惯常是多均衡的产物：一旦多数人在某选项上形成网络，转向虽整体更优，个体却先承担协调成本，于是次优被锁定，即路径依赖。破解靠聚点（焦点、政策、标准）把预期对齐，如政府指定充电接口或汇率锚。
detailEn: Unlike the prisoner's dilemma, in coordination games private and collective interests align; the issue is which way to coordinate. Keyboards (QWERTY), standards, units and habits often stem from multiple equilibria: once a network forms on one option, switching—even if collectively better—makes each bear cost first, so the suboptimal is locked in, i.e. path dependence. Escape needs a focal point—an expectation anchor—to align everyone, e.g. government-mandated charging plugs or a currency peg.
example: 早期打字速度取决于避免机械杆卡键的 QWERTY 布局，即便它并非最优，因惯性沿用至今。
exampleEn: QWERTY was set to jam fewer typebars, not for speed; the inertia keeps it alive despite suboptimal layout.
takeaways: 越多人用越有用（网络效应）常把标准锁死在并非最优的那一个。
打破锁定需要有人先对齐预期，政策、焦点或临界质量都可能触发切换。
takeawaysEn: The more who use it, the more useful it gets—locking a non-optimal standard.
Breaking lock-in needs expectation alignment; policy, a focal point, or critical mass can trigger a switch.

sources.label: 谢林《冲突的策略》；阿瑟关于报酬递增与路径依赖
sources.labelEn: Schelling, The Strategy of Conflict; Arthur on increasing returns and path dependence

name: 信号博弈
oneLiner: 信息一方靠发出“昂贵到只有真货才发得起”的信号来自证，均衡能否成立全看造假成本够不够高。
oneLinerEn: An informed party proves itself by sending a signal too costly for a fake to afford; whether the equilibrium holds depends entirely on fakes finding it unaffordable.
detail: 斯彭斯（1973）在逆向选择之外补上“信号”这一腿：能力强的人更愿（也更负担得起）读多年书，于是学历把类型分开。关键在于信号必须昂贵且对不同人有不同成本，低能力者模仿不划算，才能形成“分离均衡”；若成本差不够大，所有人挤到同一档就是“混同均衡”，信号失效。与“筛检”相对——这里是信息方主动出价自证。学历究竟是提升能力（人力资本）还是仅暴露既有能力，正是它最激烈的争论。
detailEn: Spence (1973) adds 'signaling' alongside adverse selection: the more able are keener and better placed to afford years of schooling, so credentials sort types. The crux is that a signal must be costly, and cost more for low types, so mimicking doesn't pay—only then does a 'separating equilibrium' arise; if cost differences are too small, everyone crowds into one tier, a 'pooling equilibrium', and the signal fails. It is the mirror of 'screening'—here the informed side bids to reveal itself. Whether schooling raises ability (human capital) or merely exposes it is the sharpest dispute around it.
example: 厂商敢给长期免费质保，是因为只有对自己质量真有信心的好货才付得起坏品赔付，消费者据此把它与劣质品区分开。
exampleEn: A firm dares to offer a long free warranty because only a genuinely good product can afford to pay out defects, so buyers tell it from the shoddy.
takeaways: 信号可信与否取决于成本结构，而非口头声明——“烧钱”本身才是内容。
当模仿成本下降（文凭泛滥），信号贬值，市场退回逆向选择。
takeawaysEn: A signal's credibility rests on cost structure, not talk—the 'burning of money' is the message.
When imitation gets cheap (credential inflation), the signal degrades and the market slides back to adverse selection.

sources.label: 斯彭斯《劳动力市场信号》（1973）

name: 最后通牒与独裁者博弈
oneLiner: 一人提议怎么分钱、另一人可拒绝（双方都归零），结果“太少的钱也会被拒”，戳破了纯自利假设。
oneLinerEn: One proposes a split, the other can reject it (both get nothing)—yet 'too little gets rejected', puncturing the pure-self-interest assumption.
detail: 古斯等（1982）用一笔小钱实验：按子博弈精炼均衡，提议者只给一元、响应者也该接受（一元胜过零）。现实里过低的分成常被拒，人们宁愿自己少拿也要惩罚“不公平”。去掉拒绝权的“独裁者博弈”中，多数仍会给对方留一点，只是幅度小得多。这为公平偏好、报复与“昂贵信号式的强硬”提供了可复现证据，也催生了 Fehr–Schmidt 等不平等规避模型。限度在于：小额、一次性、匿名实验对真实市场谈判的外部效度有限，文化与制度差异显著。
detailEn: Guth et al. (1982) split a small stake: subgame-perfect equilibrium says the proposer offers the least and the responder accepts (something beats nothing). In fact low offers are often rejected—people pay to punish 'unfairness'. Even in the 'dictator game', where the responder can't reject, most still leave the other something, just far less. This gives reproducible evidence for fairness preferences, spite and 'costly tough signalling', and spawned inequity-aversion models (Fehr-Schmidt). Its limits: small, one-shot, anonymous lab stakes generalize weakly to real bargaining, and culture and institution matter a lot.
example: 两人分一百元，甲提议只给乙五元，乙宁可两人都拿零也拒绝——理性模型预测不了这份“争气钱”。
exampleEn: Splitting 100, A offers B just 5; B rejects so both get nothing, preferring to 'save face'—something the rational model can't predict.
takeaways: 人会为惩罚不公平付出真实代价，纯自利假设在分配场景系统性失灵。
拒绝权显著抬高平均分成——谈判力（而非利他）也塑造“公平”。
takeawaysEn: People pay real costs to punish unfairness; pure self-interest fails systematically in allocation settings.
The power to reject markedly raises average shares—bargaining leverage, not altruism, also shapes 'fairness'.

sources.label: 古斯、施密特伯格、施瓦茨《最后通牒谈判的实验分析》（1982）
sources.labelEn: Guth, Schmittberger & Schwarze, An Experimental Analysis of Ultimatum Bargaining

name: 稳定匹配与延迟接受
oneLiner: 没有价格的市场（住培、择校、捐肾）靠算法配对，目标是让没人宁愿抛下现配去私下双宿。
oneLinerEn: Priceless markets (residency, school choice, kidney swaps) are matched by algorithm, aiming so no pair would rather ditch their matches to elope together.
detail: 盖尔与沙普利（1962）证明：在双方各有偏好的两列匹配里，存在“稳定”解——不存在一男一女（或医院与医生）双双宁愿弃当前对象而互选。延迟接受算法让一方逐轮申请、另一方暂优后择优保留、末轮定盘，且对提出申请的一方“说真话最优”。罗斯（1980s–90s）把它接入美国住院医匹配、肾脏交换与择校，2012 年获诺奖。核心洞见：当价格不能出清（伦理或管制禁止），机制设计能替代价格，但会留下“哪一方提申请”的策略红利。
detailEn: Gale and Shapley (1962) showed that in two-sided matching with preferences a 'stable' outcome exists—no man and woman (or hospital and doctor) both prefer to abandon their matches for each other. The deferred-acceptance algorithm has one side apply round by round while the other tentatively holds its best, settling at the end; it is strategy-proof (truthful is optimal) for the applying side. Roth (1980s–90s) wired it into U.S. residency matching, kidney exchange and school choice, earning the 2012 Nobel. The core insight: where prices can't clear (ethics or rules forbid them), mechanism design substitutes for price—but leaves a strategic edge to whichever side proposes.
example: 美国住院医匹配中，学生按真实意愿排序申报、医院择优暂留，避免了过去“抢人大战”里双方都谎报偏好、提前私签的混乱。
exampleEn: In U.S. residency matching, students rank honestly and apply, hospitals hold the best tentatively, ending the old scramble where both lied about preferences and signed deals too early.
takeaways: 价格被禁止时，算法能替代它达成“稳定”，但设计的细节决定红利归谁。
对弱势或急着成交的一方，“先申请者”规则往往是它唯一可用的筹码。
takeawaysEn: When price is barred, an algorithm can deliver 'stability' in its place—but design details decide who captures the surplus.
For the weaker or more urgent side, the 'who-proposes' rule is often its only usable lever.

sources.label: 盖尔、沙普利《大学录取与婚姻稳定》（1962）；罗斯的实践
sources.labelEn: Gale & Shapley, College Admissions and the Stability of Marriage; Roth's practice

name: 逆向归纳与可信承诺
oneLiner: 从终局往回推最优，常推出“一开始就摊牌”，于是先自缚手脚（破釜沉舟）反而成了优势。
oneLinerEn: Reasoning optimal moves from the end backward often yields 'showdown at once'—so binding your own hands (burning the bridges) becomes an advantage.
detail: 有限序贯博弈用逆向归纳求解：先看最后一步谁怎么走，再倒推前一步。蜈蚣博弈显示这会很反直觉——两人轮流“继续/收手”，每多一轮总收益更高，但倒推到尽头竟是第一步就收手。原因是“我下一轮会合作”并不可信，理性人会在最后背叛，于是合作在起点就崩。谢林的正解是可信承诺：主动删掉自己的退路（烧船、立约、把决定权交给规则），让威胁或合作变得可信。这解释了央行独立性、债务上限、自动售货机不接受砍价等“自缚”设计的价值。
detailEn: Finite sequential games are solved by backward induction: fix the last mover's best step, then unwind. The centipede game makes this counterintuitive—two players alternate 'continue/take', each extra round raising total gains, yet unwinding to the very end says take on move one. Because 'I'll cooperate next round' isn't credible—a rational player defects at the last node—cooperation collapses at the start. Schelling's fix is the credible commitment: deliberately deleting your own escape (burn the boats, pre-contract, hand the decision to a rule) so a threat or promise becomes believable. This is the value of 'self-binding' designs like central-bank independence, debt ceilings, or a vending machine that won't haggle.
example: 科尔特斯登陆后焚船，把“可撤退”从对手与士兵的选择集里物理删除，让“只能前进打赢”成为可信承诺。
exampleEn: After landing, Cortes burned his ships, physically deleting 'retreat' from the choice set of foes and troops alike, making 'we can only press on and win' a credible commitment.
takeaways: 理性倒推会摧毁合作；能可信地限制自己的未来选项，反而赢得当下的信任。
制度（独立央行、自动规则、第三方托管）本质是把承诺“写死”的技术。
takeawaysEn: Rational unwind destroys cooperation; credibly constraining your future options wins present trust.
Institutions (independent central banks, automatic rules, escrow) are technologies for writing a commitment down.

sources.label: 谢林《冲突的战略》；罗森塔尔蜈蚣博弈（1981）
sources.labelEn: Schelling, The Strategy of Conflict; Rosenthal's centipede game
